name: Field Guide to Edible Plants
description: a battered field guide, pages stained with berry juice
flavor: Someone loved this book. Margins full of notes.

name: Foxfire Journal
description: a handwritten journal, cooking stains on every page
flavor: Recipes and failures. Day 43: FINALLY got the acorns right.

name: Trapper Handbook
description: a slim volume on snares and deadfalls
flavor: Diagrams of knots. Check at dawn. Always.

name: Medicinal Plants of the Southeast
description: a clinical guide, precise illustrations
flavor: Dosages and warnings. Whoever owned this was careful.

name: System Field Manual: Edible Fauna (Rev. 3)
description: a System-printed pamphlet, cheerful pictograms, one page glued shut
flavor: REV. 3 NOTES: The small green jumpers are FRIEND-SHAPED. They are not friends. They are FOOD-SHAPED. We apologize for Rev. 2. The glued page is glued for your safety.

name: Smoke and Salt: A Meat-Keeper's Notes
description: a grease-spotted notebook, smoke worked into the binding
flavor: Grease-spotted pages. 'Day 11: the smokehouse worked. Day 12: the raccoons found the smokehouse. Day 13: smoked raccoon.'

name: A Forager's Almanac of the Turned Year
description: a hand-bound almanac, moon charts corrected in red ink
flavor: 'The moons moved. Everything fruits a month late now. Don't argue with the sky — write it down.'

name: The Scattered Ledger
description: a water-warped ledger, names and tallies in three different hands
flavor: Forty-one names, each with a debt or a debt owed. The last page just says: start again.

name: System Field Manual: Small Game (Rev. 5)
description: a System-printed pamphlet, cheerful pictograms, one page chewed by something
flavor: REV. 5 NOTES: The spring-pole method has been DEEMED SPORTING. The pole does the work. You do the waiting. Waiting is the hard part. We believe in you.

name: Basketry for Beginners
description: a library discard, due-date card stamped 2019, someone's practice weave tucked inside
flavor: Someone checked this out in 2019 and never brought it back. The librarian's stamp says OVERDUE in red. There is no librarian now. There is no overdue.

name: The Smokehouse Ledger
description: a smoke-stained account book, columns of dates, weights, and weather
flavor: 'Day 9: hung the venison too low. Day 10: the dog is a genius. Day 11: hung it higher.'

name: Notes of a Country Butcher
description: a spiral notebook, forty years of diagrams in pencil, blood on the edges
flavor: 'Respect the animal. Waste nothing. The gut pile feeds the woods that fed you.'

name: The Hedge-Witch's Herbarium
description: a hand-stitched herbarium, pressed leaves between every page
flavor: 'Yarrow stops the bleed. Plantain draws the sting. Jewelweed owes the poison ivy a debt -- rub it on within the hour.'

name: Night Walker's Guide
description: a slim pamphlet, ink smudged, margins full of moon phases
flavor: Everything worth catching is out at night. So is everything that catches you. The pamphlet is honest about both.

name: Birds of the Scattering
description: a watercolored bird guide, species from three counties crossed out, new ones inked in
flavor: Someone crossed out the migration maps and wrote 'GONE?' in the margins. The feeding-behavior notes are better than the pictures.

name: The Fisher's Ledger
description: a waterproof logbook, knots and rigs sketched between tallies
flavor: 'June 3: trotline lost to a turtle. June 4: ate the turtle. June 5: new trotline, deeper set.'

name: Mend and Make Do
description: a pamphlet on repairs, corners curled, held together with its own advice
flavor: Rule one: a cord is a rope that hasn't decided yet. Rule two: nothing with a handle is truly broken.

name: The Gardener's Winter
description: a seed-company almanac with forty years of handwritten corrections
flavor: Printed dates: useless. Marginalia: everything. 'The onions don't care what the packet says.'

name: The Nut Gatherer's Handbook
description: a forester's guide, shell fragments pressed between the pages
flavor: Every chapter ends with the same note about patience. The pressed shell fragments still smell faintly of rain.

name: A Field Guide to the Thicket
description: a trail-club pamphlet, thorn tears mended with electrical tape
flavor: Taped thorn tears on every other page. 'If you come out clean, you didn't go deep enough.'

name: Roots & Reasons
description: a schoolteacher's notebook, drawings in colored pencil
flavor: Colored-pencil drawings, each dated like a small portrait. The teacher signed every page.

name: The Late-Summer Herbarium
description: a pressed-flower collection with a botanist's typed labels
flavor: Latin names, pressed stems, and one page that only says DO NOT RUSH in large letters.

name: The Small-Game Hunter's Almanac
description: a dog-eared pamphlet, acorn doodles in the margins
flavor: Acorn doodles in the margins. 'The woods are a pantry with legs.'

name: The Fur-Taker's Winter Journal
description: a trapper's ledger with a frost-cracked cover
flavor: 'Check the line before the freeze. Check it again after.' The handwriting gets shakier as winter deepens.

name: System Field Manual: Predator Sign (Rev. 2)
description: a System-printed pamphlet, track diagrams in cheerful green
flavor: REV. 2 NOTES: Tracks are QUESTIONS, not answers. A big print and an empty belly are a bad combination. Walk LOUD. We mean it.

name: The Pond-Watcher's Notes
description: a damp notebook with a heron sketched on every third page
flavor: A heron sketched on every third page, each one more patient than the last.

name: The Night Shift Notebook
description: a third-shift worker's notebook, written by headlamp
flavor: Written by headlamp on night shifts. 'The dark is busy. You're just not invited to the schedule meeting.'

name: Big Game, Small Margin
description: a hunter's memoir, one chapter per scar
flavor: One chapter per scar. The shortest chapter is titled 'The Boar.' The longest is 'The Fence.'
